sections.title: Advanced Strategy for Level 3 Figure Series
sections.content: In Level 3, multiple complex rules operate simultaneously. Step 1: Identify all elements and track them separately. Step 2: Examine movement, rotation, and shape transformation individually. Step 3: Check whether the pattern is increasing, decreasing, or following a geometric progression. Step 4: Identify the roles of the center, corners, and axes. Step 5: Compare 3–4 figures to confirm the rule.

sections.title: Increasing or Decreasing Logic
sections.content: Step 1: Observe the movement distance or rotation degree of an element. Step 2: Check whether it increases or decreases in each step. Step 3: Determine whether the increase follows an arithmetic or geometric pattern. Step 4: Predict the next step using the same progression. Example: If an element moves 1 position, then 2, then 4, the next step will be 8 positions.

sections.title: Element Substitution Pattern
sections.content: Step 1: Identify which shape is moving. Step 2: Check whether the shape changes when it reaches the center. Step 3: Identify the new shape based on the number of sides or structural change. Step 4: Understand the shape replacement rule. Example: A triangle reaching the center may transform into a square, and a square may change into a pentagon.

sections.title: Complex 3D Series
sections.content: Step 1: Identify the faces and orientation of the object. Step 2: Determine the axis of rotation (horizontal, vertical, or diagonal). Step 3: Check whether rotation occurs around different axes in each step. Step 4: Track the position of faces. Step 5: Identify the next orientation following the same sequence. Example: A face of a cube may move from the top to the front and then to the right side.

sections.title: Multiple Rule Combination
sections.content: Step 1: Identify movement, rotation, and shape changes separately. Step 2: Check whether these rules operate simultaneously. Step 3: Verify each rule step by step. Step 4: Ensure the final figure satisfies all rules together. Example: A symbol may rotate while its shape also transforms.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Focusing on only one pattern when multiple rules are present. 2. Failing to identify geometric progression. 3. Ignoring axes during 3D rotation analysis. 4. Missing the shape substitution rule.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Level 3 figure series involve complex rules such as movement, rotation, and transformation. Patterns like increasing or decreasing movement, center-based shape substitution, and multi-axis 3D rotation are common. A systematic analysis of all elements is essential to identify the correct answer.

tricks.title: Movement Doubling Trick
tricks.explanation: If movement increases rapidly, check for a geometric progression pattern.

tricks.title: Rotation Degree Check
tricks.explanation: Count the rotation degree at each step.

tricks.title: Center Replacement Rule
tricks.explanation: Sometimes the center position triggers a special transformation rule.
tricks.example: A triangle may become a square when it reaches the center.

tricks.title: Sides Progression Trick
tricks.explanation: Shapes may transform according to an increasing number of sides.

tricks.title: 3D Face Tracking
tricks.explanation: Mentally track the faces of cubes or 3D blocks.
tricks.example: The top face may become the front face in the next step.

tricks.title: Axis Identification Method
tricks.explanation: Identify whether the rotation occurs along the vertical or horizontal axis.
tricks.example: A cube may roll toward the right side.

tricks.title: Layer Movement Trick
tricks.explanation: In multi-faced objects, only one layer may rotate.
tricks.example: The upper layer of a cube may rotate clockwise.

tricks.title: Rule Combination Check
tricks.explanation: If one rule is unclear, check for a combination of two rules.
tricks.example: A shape may rotate while the number of sides also increases.
